question: At what point in the patient's hospital stay should discharge planning ideally begin?

options.A: Two hours before leaving
options.B: After arriving back home
options.C: During the final doctor's round
options.D: On the day of admission

explanation: Discharge planning starts early so the care team has enough time to arrange equipment, home support, and education before the patient leaves. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h6)

question: Which group of people suffers the most from poor environmental hygiene?

options.A: Teenagers in secondary schools
options.B: Children under five years old
options.C: Middle-aged office workers
options.D: Healthy young adult athletes

explanation: You're right! Little ones are still developing their immunity, making them extra vulnerable to severe dehydration from tummy bugs. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T9#GNS112_U5_T9_h6)

question: A first-time mom has a long second stage of labor with a large baby. What is she most at risk for down there?

options.A: Severe muscle stretching and potential nerve injury
options.B: Immediate permanent tightening of the levator ani
options.C: Hypertrophy and increased muscle strength
options.D: Complete ossification of the pelvic ligaments

explanation: Exactly. Extended pushing and a big baby can really overwork and overstretch the pelvic floor muscles and nerves. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T12#GNS121_U5_T12_h3)

question: What is one of the most common ways nurses accidentally get needle-stick injuries on duty?

options.A: Transporting bins during morning shift changes
options.B: Recapping used injection needles
options.C: Using plastic syringes instead of glass
options.D: Emptying safety boxes when they are full

explanation: Spot on. Trying to guide a cap back onto a used needle puts your fingers right in the line of fire. Best practice? Never recap needles! [learn more](GNS122_U5_T1#GNS122_U5_T1_h3)

question: How can you tell the difference between morning joint stiffness in osteoarthritis versus inflammatory arthritis?

options.A: Osteoarthritis stiffness only affects the upper body joints.
options.B: Osteoarthritis stiffness never happens in the morning hours.
options.C: Osteoarthritis stiffness usually lasts less than thirty minutes.
options.D: Osteoarthritis stiffness gets worse the more the person moves.

explanation: Joint stiffness from wear-and-tear arthritis is brief after waking up, whereas inflammatory arthritis causes stiffness lasting an hour or more. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h3)

question: Why do blood vessels become more permeable during the early stages of acute inflammation?

options.A: To allow protective fluid and white blood cells to enter the tissue
options.B: To cause immediate clotting and seal off the skin surface
options.C: To flush harmful bacteria directly back into the major arteries
options.D: To prevent any blood from reaching the injured site

explanation: Increased permeability lets immune cells and proteins escape the bloodstream to fight the infection at the tissue level. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the very first thing you should do if you accidentally get poked by a needle?

options.A: Take a strong dose of broad antibiotics
options.B: Apply a tight tourniquet above the elbow
options.C: Fill out an incident report form for HR
options.D: Wash the puncture site with soap and water

explanation: Quickly washing the spot with soap and water helps flush away germs before they can enter your bloodstream. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h7)

question: Which of these is a key feature of passive immunization?

options.A: It takes several weeks to start working
options.B: It stimulates long-lasting immune memory
options.C: It uses live, virulent disease strains
options.D: It provides immediate but temporary protection

explanation: Passive immunity is like borrowing an umbrella—you get instant protection when you need it, but it doesn't last forever because your body didn't make the memory cells. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T11#GNS313_U2_T11_h3)

question: Which skin sign is most often seen in patients with a low platelet count (thrombocytopenia)?

options.A: Yellow discoloration of the skin
options.B: Severe dry and peeling patches
options.C: Petechiae and easy bruising
options.D: Widespread painful blistering

explanation: Without enough platelets to patch tiny leaks in blood vessels, patients easily get tiny red dots (petechiae) and bruises from minor bumps. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T2#GNS311_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why do nurses look at a patient's skin as a mirror of their inner health?

options.A: Skin changes often appear before systemic disease symptoms show
options.B: The skin controls all chemical reactions in the human body
options.C: External skin temperature dictates core metabolic rate completely
options.D: Internal organs directly push pigment through the dermal layers

explanation: The skin often gives us early warning signs. Changes in color, texture, or rashes can show up before other internal sickness symptoms even start! [learn more](GNS213_U5_T2#GNS213_U5_T2_h1)

question: A patient in her second trimester feels the baby move for the first time and feels much more connected. What is this milestone called?

options.A: Quickening
options.B: Nesting
options.C: Ambivalence
options.D: Couvade

explanation: Well done! Quickening is that magical moment when fetal movement makes the pregnancy feel truly real. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T004#GNS226_U2_T004_h2)

question: What crucial warning must you give a patient who takes daily anti-seizure medication?

options.A: Only take the pills on days when you feel a headache coming on
options.B: Never stop taking the medication suddenly without consulting your doctor
options.C: Stop the medication immediately if you go one week without a seizure
options.D: Take a double dose whenever you feel stressed or tired

explanation: Spot on! Quitting anti-seizure meds abruptly can trigger dangerous rebound seizures or status epilepticus. Always taper safely with a doctor's guidance. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T10#GNS222_U4_T10_h8)

question: Why do we track wastage rates on our monthly injection safety form?

options.A: It automatically increases the monthly government drug allocation
options.B: It helps managers justify future procurement requests and reduce loss
options.C: It replaces the need for keeping a physical pharmacy inventory
options.D: It punishes nurses who accidentally drop sterile items

explanation: Spot on! Tracking broken or wasted items shows management where supplies are leaking, helping us order better next time. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h2)

question: When a female condom is inserted properly, where does its closed end sit?

options.A: Over the cervix
options.B: Around the base of the bladder
options.C: Against the labia majora
options.D: Inside the fallopian tube

explanation: You got it! The closed end goes deep inside to rest right over the cervix, much like a diaphragm does. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T016#GNS226_U6_T016_h2)

question: What is the main goal of conservative management (non-surgical care) for a mild kidney injury?

options.A: Permanently stopping all urine production from both kidneys
options.B: Repairing the kidney capsule immediately via emergency open surgery
options.C: Dissolving internal blood clots with high-dose oral anticoagulants
options.D: Allowing the organ to heal naturally through close monitoring and bed rest

explanation: For minor injuries, the body is amazing at healing itself! Conservative care just means resting and watching the patient closely without rushing into surgery. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T10#GNS213_U4_T10_h6)

question: Why does a hospital admission often disrupt a patient's ability to meet basic human needs?

options.A: Hospital environments completely eliminate stress
options.B: Patients no longer care about their personal health
options.C: Familiar daily routines and independence are interrupted
options.D: Healthcare providers automatically handle all needs instantly

explanation: Being in an unfamiliar hospital setting takes away a person's normal independence, making basic tasks harder to manage alone. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h1)

question: How should you communicate updates to the worried family of a critically ill patient?

options.A: Giving all information through a written notebook only
options.B: Speaking very quickly so they do not interrupt
options.C: Using clear, simple language without heavy medical jargon
options.D: Refusing to answer questions until visiting hours end

explanation: Families under stress need kindness and clarity. Dropping heavy medical terms just confuses them—keep it simple and reassuring! [learn more](GNS221_U4_T1#GNS221_U4_T1_h7)

question: What does the legal principle 'if it is not documented, it was not done' mean for a community health nurse?

options.A: Unrecorded care has no legal proof in a court or disciplinary hearing
options.B: Nurses must write down every single word a client speaks all day
options.C: Clients can refuse to pay if their chart lacks a doctor's stamp
options.D: Verbal reports to relatives completely replace written case notes

explanation: In legal investigations, courts rely solely on written records; unrecorded interventions cannot be proven to have taken place. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h2)

question: Why is carrying twins or triplets automatically tagged as a high-risk pregnancy?

options.A: The maternal body experiences much greater physiological strain.
options.B: The mother cannot produce breast milk after birth.
options.C: It always ends in a surgical delivery before 30 weeks.
options.D: Chromosomal abnormalities never happen in twins.

explanation: Brilliant! Carrying more than one baby puts a lot of extra workload on the mother's heart, kidneys, and body systems. It's totally normal for us to monitor these mums extra closely! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T018#GNS226_U2_T018_h1)

question: You are getting a stroke survivor ready to go home. What is the best way to involve the family?

options.A: Teach them safe transfer techniques and assess their coping abilities
options.B: Assume they already know how to handle home therapy without guidance
options.C: Tell them to hire paid nurses so they do not have to do any work
options.D: Instruct them to isolate the patient to prevent any accidental injuries

explanation: Giving families practical skills and making sure they feel ready keeps everyone safe and lowers stress at home. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T6#GNS123_U6_T6_h3)

question: Which of these does NOT normally change the incidence of a disease in a population?

options.A: The introduction of better diagnostic testing tools
options.B: The total number of historical hospital building designs
options.C: Environmental changes affecting vector breeding
options.D: Mass immunization and vaccination campaigns

explanation: Correct! Hospital architecture won't directly stop or spread infections the way vaccines or environmental changes do. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T11#GNS313_U1_T11_h5)

question: What key details should a nurse document after speaking with a returning defaulter?

options.A: A list of grocery items the client purchased that morning
options.B: The exact cost of transport the client paid to reach the town
options.C: The personal opinions of the nurse regarding the client's family
options.D: The reason for missing appointments and the new plan agreed upon

explanation: Good records capture why they missed visits and the agreed care plan, ensuring smooth continuity of care no matter who is on duty next. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T025#GNS226_U6_T025_h7)

question: A nurse tells a doctor: 'The patient's blood pressure is dropping and urine output has stopped.' Which part of SBAR is this?

options.A: Background
options.B: Recommendation
options.C: Situation
options.D: Documentation

explanation: Describing what is happening right at this exact moment is the 'Situation' part of SBAR. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h5)

question: Which rheumatic condition happens when uric acid crystals build up in the joints?

options.A: Gout
options.B: Osteoarthritis
options.C: Fibromyalgia
options.D: Rheumatoid arthritis

explanation: Gout occurs when excess uric acid forms needle-like crystals in the joints, triggering sudden and very painful flare-ups. Drinking plenty of water and watching diet helps! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T12#GNS222_U1_T12_h3)

question: Why is it smart to adjust alarm limits on a portable monitor for each specific patient?

options.A: The machine will refuse to record data without personalized input
options.B: Standard defaults are illegal to use in modern hospitals
options.C: Customizing limits stops the battery from draining too quickly
options.D: Factory defaults may be unsafe or cause unnecessary alarm fatigue

explanation: Generic settings can either miss a real problem or beep constantly for no reason (alarm fatigue). Tailoring it to the patient keeps everyone sane and safe! [learn more](GNS212_U4_T10#GNS212_U4_T10_h4)

question: What does a positive Babinski sign (toes fanning up) usually mean in an adult patient?

options.A: Normal peripheral nerve function
options.B: Dehydration and low blood pressure
options.C: Upper motor neuron damage
options.D: Severe vitamin deficiency

explanation: In babies, fanning toes are normal. But in adults, an upward Babinski reflex is a red flag pointing to upper motor neuron injury. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T4#GNS222_U3_T4_h6)

question: A doctor prescribes a proton pump inhibitor to a patient with a stomach ulcer. What is the goal of this medicine?

options.A: Reduced stomach acid production to promote ulcer healing
options.B: Increased release of bile to speed up fat digestion
options.C: Stimulation of the vagus nerve to increase appetite
options.D: Enhanced production of mucus by goblet cells

explanation: By shutting down those acid pumps, the stomach environment becomes less acidic, giving the sore tissue a chance to rest and heal up nicely. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T12#GNS121_U1_T12_h7)

question: What warning signs should you teach a patient to report right away after going home from a dilation?

options.A: Mild scratchy throat sensation
options.B: Slight fatigue from the sedation
options.C: Temporary change in voice pitch
options.D: Fever and severe worsening pain

explanation: A little throat scratchiness is totally normal after having tools passed down. But fever and severe, getting-worse pain mean infection or a tear, which need immediate care. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T19#GNS212_U1_T19_h7)

question: Why should you avoid tilting an infant's head too far back when opening their airway?

options.A: It completely stops spontaneous breathing
options.B: It always causes immediate cervical spine fractures
options.C: The flexible trachea can kink and cause an obstruction
options.D: It makes it impossible to check the pulse

explanation: An infant's windpipe is soft and flexible. If you tilt their head back too far (hyperextension), the airway actually kinks shut like a bent garden hose! [learn more](GNS212_U2_T3#GNS212_U2_T3_h4)

question: As a nurse, why is it better to approach cultural practices with understanding rather than harsh judgment?

options.A: Harsh judgment makes patients distrustful and avoids healthcare access
options.B: Cultural practices are legally protected by the federal government
options.C: Patients will report the nurse to local traditional leaders
options.D: Nurses lack the authority to question community traditions

explanation: Spot on! When patients feel attacked or judged, they tend to hide their practices and stay away from clinics when they really need help. Warmth builds trust! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T1#GNS312_U1_T1_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of writing clinical notes in home health care?

options.A: To provide reading material for family members during the evening
options.B: To replace verbal handoff reports between incoming and outgoing shifts
options.C: To serve as a legal record and ensure continuity of care among team members
options.D: To prove to the patient that the nurse visited their home on schedule

explanation: Spot on! Good documentation keeps the whole healthcare team on the same page and serves as a reliable legal record of the care you provided. Keep up the good charting habits! [learn more](GNS324_U1_T6#GNS324_U1_T6_h7)

question: When is rabies post-exposure prophylaxis necessary after an animal bite?

options.A: Only if the human victim shows signs of neurological confusion
options.B: If the patient has not received a tetanus shot within the past year
options.C: When the animal is high-risk and unavailable for observation or testing
options.D: Whenever any household pet breaks the skin during playful activity

explanation: If a high-risk animal cannot be tested or watched for signs of rabies, we don't take chances—rabies prophylaxis is started right away. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T11#GNS221_U3_T11_h5)

question: What is the term when a brain injury causes a client to completely ignore one entire side of their body or room?

options.A: Apraxia
options.B: Unilateral neglect
options.C: Global amnesia
options.D: Expressive aphasia

explanation: Unilateral neglect can feel baffling to the client—their brain literally forgets that one side of the world (or their own body) exists. As nurses, we help bridge that gap! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T22#GNS222_U3_T22_h5)

question: What actually is sepsis?

options.A: The initial stage of viral reproduction in a host cell
options.B: A localized skin reaction caused by fungal overgrowth
options.C: A systemic, life-threatening response to an infection
options.D: A normal immune reaction during the prodromal phase

explanation: Correct! Sepsis happens when an infection gets out of hand, triggering a severe, dangerous full-body inflammatory response that needs emergency care. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h7)

question: A patient with a history of heavy drinking suddenly looks confused and has trouble moving their eyes. What is the most likely condition?

options.A: Alzheimer dementia
options.B: Korsakoff syndrome
options.C: Wernicke encephalopathy
options.D: Parkinson disease

explanation: That classic mix of confusion, eye movement problems, and a history of heavy alcohol use is a textbook warning sign for acute Wernicke encephalopathy. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T8#GNS222_U4_T8_h3)

question: Why is it impossible to make human skin completely germ-free during a surgical scrub?

options.A: Soap cannot touch the outer layer of skin
options.B: Scrubs are only meant to wash away dirt
options.C: The sink water is never hot enough to kill germs
options.D: Germs hide deep inside hair roots and oil glands

explanation: Think of it like tiny hiding spots! Microbes live deep down in skin structures like hair follicles, making total sterilization impossible. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h1)

question: Why do the kidneys often take a hit during prolonged body-wide asphyxia?

options.A: Lactic acid crystals block the small ureter tubes
options.B: They absorb too much carbon dioxide from the blood
options.C: They experience severe reduction in blood perfusion
options.D: The kidneys overproduce urine to flush out toxins

explanation: When the body runs low on oxygen, it goes into survival mode, pulling blood away from the kidneys and skin to protect the brain and heart. Sadly, this leaves the kidneys starved and vulnerable to damage. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T1#GNS112_U7_T1_h7)

question: Why does our body reabsorb most digestive fluids further down the intestines?

options.A: To stop bacteria from growing in the large intestine
options.B: To prevent severe dehydration from fluid loss
options.C: To recycle digestive enzymes for chewing food
options.D: To keep the stool completely liquid at all times

explanation: Our body pours liters of fluid into the gut every day! Reclaiming that water lower down is super important so we don't dry out. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T11#GNS121_U1_T11_h1)

question: Why is taking off your PPE in the correct, specific order so important?

options.A: To ensure the equipment can be washed and reused for the next shift
options.B: To prevent transferring trapped pathogens from the gear onto your skin
options.C: To prevent the plastic straps from snapping during disposal
options.D: To speed up the process so you can leave the isolation room faster

explanation: The outside of your PPE is covered in germs. If you take it off carelessly, you'll end up wiping those germs right onto your face or hands! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h8)

question: What lifestyle habit should you strongly advise a patient with peptic ulcer disease to give up?

options.A: Eating green leafy vegetables
options.B: Drinking clean filtered water
options.C: Engaging in light daily walking
options.D: Smoking tobacco products

explanation: Nicotine slows down how fast ulcers heal and makes them way more likely to come back. Encouraging smoking cessation is a great nursing intervention! [learn more](GNS223_U3_T1#GNS223_U3_T1_h7)

question: Why is routine clamping of a chest tube strongly discouraged when moving a patient?

options.A: It permanently ruins the plastic collection chambers of the unit
options.B: It increases the risk of severe infection at the insertion site
options.C: It can quickly cause a life-threatening tension pneumothorax
options.D: It causes the sterile water in the seal chamber to evaporate

explanation: Clamping traps air and fluid with nowhere to go. This can cause the lung to collapse rapidly, so avoid clamping unless ordered for specific tests! [learn more](GNS213_U2_T15#GNS213_U2_T15_h6)

question: Why is partner notification and treatment a must when managing STIs?

options.A: To punish individuals who engage in unprotected sexual intercourse
options.B: To determine which partner originally contracted the infection first
options.C: To prevent reinfection and break the ongoing cycle of transmission
options.D: To fulfill mandatory insurance reporting requirements for hospitals

explanation: If you treat only one partner, they will just catch the infection right back the next time they have sex. Both partners must be treated together to truly heal! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h4)

question: What is the main role of the thalamus when processing sensory information?

options.A: Act as a relay station to filter and direct signals to the cortex
options.B: Store long-term memories of painful experiences
options.C: Control the physical movement of the sensory organs
options.D: Convert mechanical waves into electrical nerve impulses

explanation: Think of the thalamus as the ultimate sorting office in the brain. It checks incoming sensory messages and routes them to the right neighborhood in the cortex for you to experience them. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T1#GNS311_U3_T1_h5)

question: What is a common trigger for autonomic dysreflexia in a patient with a spinal cord injury?

options.A: Eating a high-protein meal
options.B: Bladder distension or a full bladder
options.C: Rising from a lying position
options.D: Speaking too loudly

explanation: A distended bladder or bowel impaction sends pain signals up the spinal cord that get blocked, causing a dangerous reflex surge in blood pressure. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T4#GNS123_U6_T4_h4)

question: Which layer of the uterus gives it the strong power to push out a baby during labor?

options.A: Perimetrium
options.B: Epimetrium
options.C: Myometrium
options.D: Endometrium

explanation: Well done! The myometrium is made of thick, strong muscle that contracts powerfully during childbirth. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T3#GNS121_U5_T3_h3)

question: Which health condition is directly caused by severe protein deficiency linked to poor dietary practices?

options.A: Type 2 diabetes
options.B: Hypertension
options.C: Kwashiorkor
options.D: Peptic ulcer disease

explanation: Kwashiorkor is a severe form of malnutrition caused by lack of protein, often seen when children are fed only starchy foods because of taboos. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T9#GNS225_U6_T9_h5)

question: What makes an infectious substance fit into Category A instead of Category B?

options.A: It can cause fatal or life-threatening disease upon exposure
options.B: It is shipped in much larger liquid volumes than normal samples
options.C: It only affects animals and never poses any risk to human health
options.D: It consists solely of routine urine and stool sample containers

explanation: Category A is for the scary, high-risk stuff that can cause severe or fatal illness, so it needs extra-tough packaging. Excellent practice for clinical safety! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h2)

question: What are Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) mostly about?

options.A: Community mobility and grocery shopping
options.B: Basic self-care tasks needed for daily survival
options.C: Complex household chores and managing money
options.D: Advanced professional skills and hobbies

explanation: You've got this! ADLs are simply the fundamental things we do every day to care for ourselves, like bathing, dressing, and eating. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T5#GNS324_U3_T5_h1)

question: A patient with a history of severe bee sting allergies is preparing for rural fieldwork in Nigeria. What essential item must you ensure they carry before they leave?

options.A: Prescribed epinephrine autoinjector
options.B: Traditional herbal mud for wound dressing
options.C: A bottle of strong perfume for protection
options.D: A pair of dark-colored gardening gloves

explanation: Excellent! Anyone with a history of severe stings must always have their epinephrine autoinjector on hand to treat accidental stings instantly. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T12#GNS221_U3_T12_h8)

question: Why might private clinics push for more injections in a fee-for-service system?

options.A: Government subsidies pay hospitals more for oral pills.
options.B: Insurance companies strictly forbid giving prescriptions for tablets.
options.C: Injections and related supplies allow them to charge higher fees.
options.D: Needles and syringes are completely free for medical facilities.

explanation: Financial gain drives unnecessary injections when clinics profit from charging extra for procedural administration and supplies. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h4)

question: Which muscle group acts like a supportive hammock at the bottom of the pelvis?

options.A: Rectus abdominis muscles
options.B: Detrusor muscle group
options.C: Levator ani muscle group
options.D: Abdominal wall muscles

explanation: Think of the levator ani as a strong sling or hammock holding all your pelvic organs neatly in place. Great job! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h2)

question: A patient on bedrest after hip surgery suddenly complains of chest pain and shortness of breath. What should you suspect?

options.A: Compartment syndrome
options.B: Pulmonary embolism
options.C: Hypovolemic shock
options.D: Fat embolism syndrome

explanation: Sudden breathlessness and chest pain in someone who has been immobile scream 'pulmonary embolism.' Quick assessment and action can save a life here! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T23#GNS222_U1_T23_h5)

question: What is the normal range for intracranial pressure (ICP) in an adult?

options.A: 80 to 120 mmHg
options.B: 5 to 15 mmHg
options.C: 120 to 140 mmHg
options.D: 30 to 50 mmHg

explanation: Normal ICP stays between 5 and 15 mmHg. This keeps blood flowing nicely to the delicate brain tissues without crushing them. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T23#GNS222_U3_T23_h2)

question: Who founded the Henry Street Settlement to help shape early visiting nursing in urban America?

options.A: Mary Seacole
options.B: Clara Barton
options.C: Florence Nightingale
options.D: Lillian Wald

explanation: Lillian Wald was a true public health pioneer who started the Henry Street Settlement to bring proper healthcare to people living in crowded city tenements. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T2#GNS324_U1_T2_h2)

question: A patient tells you that both of their parents have high blood pressure and diabetes. Where should you write this?

options.A: Past medical history
options.B: History of present illness
options.C: Review of systems
options.D: Family history

explanation: Spot on! Information about blood relatives (like parents and siblings) always goes into the family history section so you can check for genetic risks. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T1#GNS123_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is the main problem when a drug loses its strength because of bad storage?

options.A: Rapid expiration of hospital staff
options.B: Treatment failure for the patient
options.C: Immediate toxic shock in the ward
options.D: Immediate change in tablet color

explanation: When drugs lose their potency, they simply won't work to heal the patient, leading to poor recovery. Always make sure storage conditions are right! [learn more](GNS125_U4_T4#GNS125_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why do we treat evaluation as an ongoing process rather than a one-time thing?

options.A: Patients prefer being tested multiple times a day
options.B: Hospital accreditation bodies require it to happen every hour
options.C: It prevents nurses from having to document patient care
options.D: It allows nurses to make continuous adjustments to care plans and learning strategies

explanation: Checking in continuously lets you catch issues early and tweak your care plan in real-time. It's all about helping your patient get better faster! [learn more](GST321_U9_T1#GST321_U9_T1_h1)

question: What is the nurse's specific job when handling a surgical consent form?

options.A: Explaining all potential surgical risks and complications in detail to the patient
options.B: Witnessing the patient's signature after confirming they understand the procedure from the surgeon
options.C: Signing the consent form on behalf of an unconscious patient without family
options.D: Deciding whether the patient is mentally fit to undergo general anesthesia

explanation: The doctor explains the surgery, but you act as the trusted witness to make sure the patient understands and is signing willingly. Teamwork! [learn more](GNS123_U1_T1#GNS123_U1_T1_h6)

question: What was a major focus of Nigeria's original 1988 National Population Policy?

options.A: Banning traditional birth attendants nationwide
options.B: Mandatory relocation of rural populations to cities
options.C: Providing free university education for all citizens
options.D: Setting a limit on the number of children per woman

explanation: Back in 1988, the policy tried to slow down rapid population growth by suggesting a specific target for how many children a woman should have. It faced a lot of cultural pushback, but that was the main strategy at the time! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T007#GNS226_U6_T007_h1)

question: Which group of symptoms strongly points to a pelvic infection (sepsis) after an unsafe abortion?

options.A: Painless vaginal bleeding and elevated blood pressure
options.B: High fever, foul-smelling discharge, and lower abdominal pain
options.C: Frequent urination, clear discharge, and normal temperature

question: How should emergency stock items on a ward be managed differently from regular supplies?

question: Why is watching a patient actually do a household task better than just asking if they can do it?

question: A patient expresses intense anger toward the nursing staff and complains about everything. What is the most likely root cause of this behavior?

question: What is the main goal of delivering an electrical shock during defibrillation?

options.A: To reset chaotic heart muscle activity and let a normal rhythm restart
options.B: To restart a completely flatlined heart during asystole

question: A patient walks out of a dark cinema into the bright afternoon sun and squints before seeing clearly. What is this quick adjustment called?

question: Why are the normal bacteria living inside your large intestine so important?

question: Why is having a naturally acidic vaginal pH so important for a patient's health?

question: Which of these is a great example of a non-drug (non-pharmacological) way to help a patient relax?

question: What strategy is often successful when working with religious leaders to stop harmful traditional customs?

question: Why must a nurse pay attention to workplace hazards even if they currently feel strong and healthy?

question: What is the main imaging test doctors use to see brain and spinal cord plaques in disseminated sclerosis?

explanation: An MRI is the gold standard here because it gives a clear picture of scarring and inflammation inside the central nervous system. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is the main tool used by nurses during labor to track progress and detect complications early?

options.A: Glucometer
options.B: Partograph

explanation: The partograph is a graphic record of labor used to monitor maternal and fetal well-being and flag prolonged labor. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h4)

question: How is a 'near miss' different from an adverse event?

options.A: A near miss is caught before reaching the patient, causing no actual harm

options.C: An adverse event is only recorded if the patient complains publicly

question: Which transmission route involves pathogens spreading via contaminated inanimate objects like door handles or instruments?

options.A: Airborne droplet transmission
options.B: Vector-borne transmission
options.C: Direct contact transmission
options.D: Indirect contact transmission

explanation: Indirect contact occurs when a susceptible host touches a surface or object that harbors infectious agents. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h3)

question: A patient comes in shaking, with a fast pulse and severe anxiety. What medical check should you prioritize first?

options.A: An underlying medical issue like a thyroid problem
options.B: The immediate onset of social anxiety disorder
options.C: A complete absence of neurotransmitter activity
options.D: A normal reaction to a new hospital environment

explanation: Always rule out the physical body first! Conditions like an overactive thyroid can mimic anxiety symptoms down to the last detail. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T10#GNS123_U3_T10_h4)

question: A patient on regular drugs mentions starting a strong herbal supplement to sleep better. As a nurse, what is your main concern?

options.A: The herb may interact with liver enzymes and alter the prescription drug level
options.B: The patient will instantly stop taking all of their prescribed medications
options.C: The patient is violating strict hospital dietary policies
options.D: The hospital will charge extra fees for documenting natural remedies

explanation: Spot on! Herbs have active chemicals that can mess with how the body processes prescribed drugs, leading to dangerous levels in the system. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T10#GNS125_U1_T10_h3)

question: Which physical sign tells you that a patient's peripheral tissues are poorly perfused?

options.A: Rapid pupillary reaction
options.B: Bounding carotid pulses
options.C: Cool and mottled extremities
options.D: Warm and flushed skin tone

question: A patient has a sudden blockage in a main coronary artery. What is the immediate danger to the heart?

options.A: The heart valves will instantly turn inside out from lack of pressure.

options.C: The heart muscle supplied by that artery will be starved of oxygen and may die.
options.D: The lungs will immediately fill with air instead of blood.

question: Why does the body need to metabolize drugs, especially fat-soluble ones?

options.A: To make fat-soluble drugs easier for the kidneys to excrete
options.B: To completely prevent medications from entering the bloodstream
options.C: To make all drugs stay inside fatty tissues forever
options.D: To turn every drug into a permanent fat-soluble storage form

explanation: Think of it this way: our kidneys love water-soluble stuff. If a drug is too fatty, the kidneys just let it circulate back. Metabolism changes it so the kidneys can easily flush it out in urine! You've got this. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T3#GNS125_U5_T3_h1)

question: A patient complains of chest pain and trouble swallowing because their food pipe is squeezing in an uncoordinated way. What is this called?

options.A: Oesophageal varices
options.B: Hiatus hernia
options.C: Oesophageal spasm
options.D: Mallory-Weiss tear

question: How does walking help a patient's digestive tract after surgery or illness?

options.A: It lowers the metabolic demand of the liver cells
options.B: It stops the stomach from producing gastric acid
options.C: It stimulates peristalsis to prevent constipation
options.D: It increases the absorption of water in the kidneys

explanation: Physical movement wakes up the bowels by encouraging wave-like muscle contractions called peristalsis, keeping digestion moving. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T3#GNS324_U6_T3_h1)

question: What is the primary job of ligaments in our joints?

options.A: To connect skeletal muscle directly to bone
options.B: To cushion the ends of bones from friction
options.C: To connect bone to bone and provide stability
options.D: To produce lubricating synovial fluid

explanation: Spot on! Ligaments are tough bands of tissue holding bones together so your joints stay stable when you move or carry weight. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T7#GNS121_U3_T7_h4)

question: What does a holistic approach mean in palliative care?

options.A: Addressing physical, emotional, and spiritual needs together
options.B: Focusing exclusively on spiritual counseling
options.C: Relying entirely on herbal remedies and local roots
options.D: Treating only the physical pain of the patient

explanation: A holistic approach looks at the *whole* person—body, mind, and spirit. We don't just treat a sore body; we care for the heart and mind too! [learn more](GNS321_U4_T2#GNS321_U4_T2_h2)

question: What does the abbreviation WASH stand for in public health programs?

options.A: Widespread Access to Safety Hormones

options.D: Wound Assessment and Surgical Health

question: In a nursing team, who holds the legal responsibility for assessing patients and planning their care?

question: What color should the nurse tell the patient their stool might appear for a few days after a barium swallow?

question: A patient feels very embarrassed and down about sexual changes after prostate surgery. How should you respond as a nurse?

options.D: Assure him that normal function always returns within twenty-four hours

question: Which cultural factor often contributes to severe maternal health issues in rural areas?

options.A: Excessive use of modern antenatal care clinics in the first trimester

options.C: Early mandatory retirement for women of childbearing age

question: What is your main duty as a nurse when treating a patient with complications from an unsafe abortion?

question: What marks the transition period of adolescence?

question: How do hormone-producing cells in the Diffuse Neuroendocrine System (DNES) differ from traditional glands?

question: Why are small fish eaten whole with their bones considered such a nutritional win?

question: Why is proper body support so important for patients who spend all day in bed?

question: Why might two different patients catch the exact same germ, yet show completely different symptoms?

question: Why is it usually unhelpful to just blame an individual nurse when an error occurs?

question: In a brain-injured patient, what does a sudden change in pupil size or reactivity usually tell you?

question: Why should hospital management always consult frontline ward nurses when planning a new ward layout?

question: When blood pressure drops too low, how does aldosterone help bring it back up?

question: Why is the "action line" on a partograph so critical for your clinical decisions?

question: Why must a food handler with a finger cut wear a brightly colored waterproof bandage?

question: Who came up with the famous five-stage model of dying and grief?

question: Which combination of vital sign changes makes up Cushing's triad (a sign of high pressure inside the brain)?

question: Why is insulin considered the preferred medication for managing diabetes during pregnancy?

question: What causes the sound often referred to as the 'death rattle' in an actively dying patient?

question: What is a major safety worry for a patient dealing with dysphagia (difficulty swallowing) after brain surgery?

question: At what point should health care waste be segregated?

question: What should you as a nurse do right away if a drug order written in the patient's chart is unclear?

question: What does a cracking or grating sound in a joint (called crepitus) usually mean?

question: Why must a patient empty their bladder right before getting a paracentesis?

question: In the Three Delays Model for maternal mortality, what does the second delay mean?

question: A client with severe hypertension asks for oral contraceptive pills. What should the nurse do during the assessment?

question: A patient expresses deep shame and refuses visitors due to faecal incontinence. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?
