options.B: It requires careful monitoring due to potential effects on the thyroid gland
options.C: It can only be administered through direct injection into the bone marrow
options.D: It completely stops all patient movement and causes heavy sedation

explanation: Spot on. Because iodide can mess with the thyroid gland if used for too long, nurses prefer safer options like guaifenesin. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T3#GNS223_U2_T3_h3)

question: A hospitalized patient has acute salpingitis with pelvic pain and a mild fever. Which nursing position helps drain pelvic fluids downward?

options.A: Ice packs applied directly to the lower abdomen
options.B: Strict bed rest flat on her back
options.C: Trendelenburg position with feet elevated
options.D: Semi-Fowler's position

explanation: Gravity is our friend here! Keeping the patient slightly upright helps infected fluids pool safely in the lower pelvis rather than spreading upward. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T24#GNS216_U5_T24_h7)

question: What do we call a cancer that starts in the epithelial tissue lining body surfaces?

options.A: Sarcoma
options.B: Myeloma
options.C: Leukemia
options.D: Carcinoma

explanation: You're doing great! Carcinomas are the most common type of cancer because they start in the skin and the cells lining our internal organs and body surfaces. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T6#GNS321_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which event is classified as an immunization error-related adverse event?

options.A: A child developing a mild fever due to an immune response
options.B: A mild allergic rash caused by an egg protein allergy
options.C: An abscess forming due to unsterile injection techniques
options.D: A baby catching an unrelated malaria infection the next day

explanation: Immunization errors happen due to mistakes in handling, preparation, or administration, such as introducing bacteria through poor aseptic technique. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h7)

question: Why must a nurse check the airway before breathing and circulation during an emergency?

options.A: A blocked airway will cause death regardless of heart function
options.B: Doctors only look at the airway during emergencies
options.C: It is a hospital rule with no medical reason
options.D: Airway assessment takes the least amount of time

explanation: Makes total sense! If air can't get through, nothing else matters because the body gets zero oxygen. Clearing the airway is always step number one. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T1#GNS221_U3_T1_h3)

question: When cancer treatment cannot cure the disease, but aims to stop tumor growth and extend life, what is this main goal called?

options.A: Palliation
options.B: Cure
options.C: Prevention
options.D: Control

explanation: You've got this! When complete cure isn't possible, 'control' is the goal—stopping the cancer from spreading further to help the patient live a longer, fuller life. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h1)

question: A patient has surgery to remove a bowel tumor just to relieve an active intestinal blockage. What type of surgery is this?

options.A: Diagnostic
options.B: Curative
options.C: Prophylactic
options.D: Palliative

explanation: Well done! Even though it's surgery, it's classified as palliative because its main job is to ease distressing symptoms (like a blockage) rather than cure the cancer itself. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h2)

question: What is meant by 'capacity building' in community health projects?

options.A: Increasing the salary of foreign NGO directors
options.B: Purchasing more vehicles for administrative travel
options.C: Building larger physical warehouses for medical drugs
options.D: Training local community members to sustain initiatives

explanation: Exactly! Capacity building is about teaching locals the skills they need to keep running their own health programs successfully. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h6)

question: What is the very first action a nurse should take with a surgical instrument immediately after a procedure is finished?

options.A: Wrap it tightly in sterile cloth for storage
options.B: Soak the instrument in strong bleach overnight
options.C: Place it directly into the clean instrument cabinet
options.D: Remove gross soil and blood to prevent drying

explanation: Wiping off heavy blood and tissue right away keeps it from drying onto the metal, which makes later cleaning much harder. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h5)

question: What is a major transport-related challenge that often contributes to maternal deaths in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive availability of fully equipped ambulances in villages
options.B: Too many doctors available at primary healthcare centers
options.C: Delays in transportation and reaching a medical facility
options.D: Immediate acceptance of patients at tertiary hospitals

explanation: Getting stuck trying to find transport to a hospital (the famous 'second delay') is a huge hurdle in saving mothers in remote areas. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h8)

question: What is the risk to a community if nurses accidentally give out heat-damaged vaccines?

options.A: The vaccines will turn a bright yellow color
options.B: Children will develop lifelong immunity faster
options.C: Outbreaks of preventable diseases can still occur
options.D: Patients will develop severe allergic reactions

explanation: A damaged vaccine won't trigger the body's immune system properly. People might think they are protected when they are actually still at risk. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T65#GNS214_U1_T65_h2)

question: A nursing school wants to help students dealing with the digital divide. What should they do first?

options.A: Lengthen the required clinical hours at the base hospital ward
options.B: Provide accessible computer labs and reliable internet access on campus
options.C: Remove all digital assignments from the nursing curriculum
options.D: Increase the difficulty of the weekly online quizzes

explanation: Setting up on-site computer labs and internet directly bridges the resource gap for students who don't have personal tech at home. Excellent problem-solving! [learn more](GST321_U8_T9#GST321_U8_T9_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of United Nations packaging requirements in healthcare?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of shipping medical laboratory supplies
options.B: To speed up the delivery time of routine blood test results
options.C: To ensure all medical specimens look identical to couriers
options.D: To prevent leaks and spills of hazardous materials during transit

explanation: These international rules are designed specifically to contain dangerous biological or chemical contents safely even if the outer box is dropped or crushed. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h1)

question: A local clinic plans to administer 4,000 curative injections over the next quarter without a waste factor. If each injection needs one syringe, how many syringes should be ordered?
explanation: Multiplying the total injection encounters by the dose per encounter without a waste factor gives the exact baseline total of 4,000. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h4)

question: What makes an auto-disable syringe different from a conventional disposable syringe?

options.A: It can be washed and sterilized multiple times safely.
options.B: It locks or breaks automatically to prevent second use.
options.C: It holds a much larger volume of liquid than any other type.
options.D: It is made entirely of soft, flexible rubber material.

explanation: Auto-disable syringes have a built-in mechanism that renders them completely unusable after one single stroke. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h2)

question: When is the best time to discuss family planning options with a patient receiving post-abortion care?

options.A: Before the patient is discharged from the clinical setting
options.B: Only after the patient experiences a second unplanned pregnancy
options.C: Refer them to a distant pharmacy without discussing options
options.D: Wait until six months have passed to avoid overwhelming them

explanation: Spot on! Bringing up family planning before discharge ensures the patient is protected against a quick repeat pregnancy while they are still connected to care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h5)

question: Which professional helps a client adapt their living space by introducing tools like customized eating utensils?

options.A: Surgeon
options.B: Pharmacologist
options.C: Radiologic technologist
options.D: Occupational therapist

explanation: Occupational therapists specialize in helping clients adapt their daily activities and living spaces to maintain their independence. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T15#GNS222_U4_T15_h5)

question: Between these two types of mouth lesions, which one carries a higher risk of turning into cancer?

options.A: Erythroplakia
options.B: Aphthous ulcer
options.C: Herpes labialis
options.D: Leukoplakia

explanation: Erythroplakia shows up as red, velvety patches and is much more likely to become malignant compared to white patches (leukoplakia). [learn more](GNS213_U3_T4#GNS213_U3_T4_h3)

question: Why do we encourage a new colostomy patient to start practicing bag changes early?

options.A: To prove the patient doesn't need emotional counseling anymore
options.B: To make the surgical belly cut heal much faster
options.C: To help the hospital nurses finish their heavy daily chores
options.D: To build self-confidence and lower worry about caring for themselves at home

explanation: You nailed it! Practicing with a nurse nearby helps patients beat their fears and master the skills they need to be independent. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h7)

question: What is the main reason nurses use fluorescein sodium eye drops?

options.A: To dilate the pupil for a deep retinal view
options.B: To kill bacteria causing severe pink eye
options.C: To highlight scratches and foreign objects on the cornea under special light
options.D: To numb the surface before checking eye pressure

explanation: Fluorescein is a brilliant diagnostic tool! It clings to damaged spots on the cornea and glows bright green under a blue light so you can easily spot tiny scratches. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h5)

question: Which nutrient is most often missing in unfortified gluten-free grain alternatives?

options.A: Sodium
options.B: Potassium
options.C: B vitamins
options.D: Vitamin C

explanation: Standard wheat products are usually fortified with B vitamins like folate, which alternative flours often lack unless added back. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T011#GNS227_U6_T011_h5)

question: What is the first-line medication of choice for treating a severe anaphylactic drug reaction?

options.A: Diphenhydramine
options.B: Hydrocortisone
options.C: Epinephrine
options.D: Albuterol

explanation: Epinephrine is the life-saving drug that must be given immediately during anaphylaxis to reverse airway swelling and raise blood pressure. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T4#GNS215_U5_T4_h7)

question: What is a crucial safety tip a nurse should share with a patient who has severe haemophilia?

options.A: Take aspirin daily to prevent unwanted blood clot formation.
options.B: Avoid contact sports and activities carrying a high risk of injury.
options.C: Use stiff-bristled toothbrushes to thoroughly clean the gums.
options.D: Stop taking prescribed factor infusions when joint pain disappears.

explanation: Safety first! Contact sports can lead to dangerous internal bleeding or painful joint bleeds for someone with haemophilia, so finding safer hobbies is key. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T10#GNS311_U2_T10_h8)

question: What is a major ethical dilemma an occupational health nurse frequently faces?

options.A: Deciding whether to do surgery without a doctor
options.B: Balancing loyalty to the employer with the duty to protect worker health and privacy
options.C: Choosing between clinical nursing and selling products
options.D: Reporting fellow nurses to criminal courts for minor errors

explanation: Spot on! Because the company pays your salary but nursing ethics demand patient privacy, it can be a tough tightrope to walk. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h8)

question: What is a crucial first step when caring for a malnourished child who also has an acute infection?

options.A: Treat the underlying infection alongside nutritional support
options.B: Restrict all oral fluids to prevent electrolyte imbalances
options.C: Discharge the child immediately for home management
options.D: Wait until the child regains full weight before giving medicines

explanation: Infections and malnutrition make a dangerous pair because sickness steals appetite and burns energy. Treating the infection right away is a life-saving priority! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T005#GNS227_U2_T005_h7)

question: What is a major advantage that barrier methods like condoms have over hormonal methods?

options.A: They never need to be replaced or bought again
options.B: Protection against sexually transmitted infections
options.C: They require no active participation during intercourse
options.D: They completely stop menstrual bleeding forever

explanation: Spot on! While hormonal methods prevent pregnancy, only barrier methods like condoms give that dual protection against STIs as well. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h2)

question: Why do maternity nurses need to know baby skull anatomy well?

options.A: It helps assess foetal position and monitor labour progress
options.B: It allows the nurse to calculate the exact date of conception
options.C: It determines whether the mother will need a blood transfusion
options.D: It prevents the need for any internal pelvic examinations

explanation: Spot on! By feeling the landmarks on the baby's head during vaginal exams, you can tell which way the baby is facing and how well labor is moving along. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T10#GNS121_U6_T10_h1)

question: Which common fungus frequently causes yeast infections on the vulva?

options.A: Neisseria gonorrhoeae
options.B: Trichomonas vaginalis
options.C: Candida albicans
options.D: Escherichia coli

explanation: Candida albicans is a fungus that normally hangs out on our bodies harmlessly, but when conditions are right, it can overgrow and cause that familiar itching and irritation. Keep up the great revision! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T6#GNS216_U5_T6_h2)

question: Why are two different medications used together in a medical abortion?

options.A: Combining them achieves a higher success rate than using either drug by itself
options.B: Using both drugs simultaneously shortens the bleeding duration by half
options.C: The second drug is needed immediately to reverse the side effects of the first
options.D: Mifepristone causes the contractions while misoprostol blocks the hormones

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! Using mifepristone first to prepare the uterus and then misoprostol to empty it works best together for a complete process. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T012#GNS226_U5_T012_h1)

question: What is a classic sign of chronic urinary schistosomiasis?

options.A: Severe chest pain
options.B: Terminal hematuria
options.C: Swollen painful joints
options.D: Jaundice and yellow eyes

explanation: As trapped parasite eggs irritate the bladder lining, blood shows up right at the very end of passing urine (terminal hematuria). A classic nursing assessment sign! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T10#GNS214_U1_T10_h4)

question: Why might a patient agree with family planning advice at the clinic, but fail to practice it at home?

options.A: The medication expires too quickly
options.B: Bad weather during the journey
options.C: Fear of community or family pressure
options.D: Lack of clean clinic floors

explanation: Spot on! Patients often feel caught between great clinical advice and the heavy cultural expectations waiting back home. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T006#GNS226_U6_T006_h1)

question: What is the main benefit of knowing basic nutrition terms at the bedside?

options.A: Calculating precise hospital food budgets
options.B: Diagnosing rare genetic disorders
options.C: Prescribing tube feeding formulas independently
options.D: Spotting early signs of nutritional decline

explanation: Spotting trouble early lets you advocate for your patient before a minor nutrition issue turns into a major clinical problem. You've got this! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T001#GNS227_U1_T001_h1)

question: Which of the following is a frequent long-term complication of poorly treated acute osteomyelitis?

options.A: Rheumatoid arthritis
options.B: Iron deficiency anemia
options.C: Type 1 diabetes mellitus
options.D: Chronic osteomyelitis

explanation: When acute bone infections are not fully eradicated, they frequently transition into long-standing chronic osteomyelitis with recurrent flare-ups. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h10)

question: Which type of immunity are we born with as our body's built-in, general defense?

options.A: Active natural immunity
options.B: Passive artificial immunity
options.C: Innate immunity
options.D: Adaptive immunity

explanation: Nice work! Innate immunity is your natural, everyday shield that you are born with—like your skin and mucous membranes. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T83#GNS214_U1_T83_h2)

question: Why is community conversation so important when trying to stop FGM in local Nigerian settings?

options.A: Traditional leaders have no influence over community behavior
options.B: Local laws forbid nurses from ever talking about reproductive health
options.C: The practice is deeply tied to cultural identity and social acceptance
options.D: Economic penalties are the only proven way to change minds

explanation: Because FGM is rooted in deep traditions and social pressure, laws alone aren't enough—we need community-wide education to change hearts and minds. You've got this! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse must do if a patient reacts badly to an IV medication?

options.A: Give an oral allergy tablet
options.B: Write down the exact time in the chart
options.C: Leave the room to find the doctor
options.D: Stop the medication infusion right away

explanation: Safety first! Stopping the drug immediately keeps any more of the bad stuff from entering the patient's body. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T4#GNS215_U5_T4_h5)

question: When the Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (RAAS) kicks in, what is its main job?

options.A: Increase blood volume and cause vasoconstriction
options.B: Decrease heart rate and promote fluid excretion
options.C: Stimulate direct potassium loss through the sweat glands
options.D: Dilate peripheral arteries and lower blood pressure

explanation: When blood pressure drops too low, RAAS comes to the rescue by tightening blood vessels and telling the kidneys to hold onto water and salt to boost pressure back up. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T6#GNS111_U2_T6_h2)

question: What is one of the biggest threats to the long-term success of mobile healthcare outreach programs?

options.A: Strict government regulations prohibiting community-level nursing practice
options.B: A complete lack of interest from community members in receiving care
options.C: Excessive availability of advanced diagnostic machinery in rural villages
options.D: Difficulty in sustaining funding and services after initial project phases end

explanation: Many great programs struggle when initial donor funds or temporary support run dry. It's a major challenge in community nursing! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T15#GNS225_U5_T15_h7)

question: What unit of measurement do electronic IV infusion pumps typically use to set fluid rates?

options.A: Liters per 24 hours
options.B: Milliliters per hour
options.C: Drops per second
options.D: Grams per minute

explanation: Infusion pumps are programmed directly in mL/hr to deliver precise fluid volumes over time. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T5#GNS125_U3_T5_h7)

question: What does sexual orientation primarily describe?

options.A: The anatomical sex assigned to a baby at birth
options.B: The social roles assigned by culture to men and women
options.C: How a person displays their internal gender feelings
options.D: A person's romantic or physical attraction to others

explanation: Sexual orientation focuses on who a person desires to be with emotionally and physically, which is separate from their own gender identity. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T1#GNS312_U4_T1_h3)

question: Which blood marker is the most specific and sensitive indicator of heart muscle damage?

options.A: Troponin
options.B: White blood cells
options.C: C-reactive protein
options.D: Serum potassium

explanation: Troponin proteins are released directly into the blood when heart muscle cells suffer ischemic injury, making them the gold standard for detecting heart attacks. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T13#GNS213_U1_T13_h2)

question: What personal protective equipment is a must when working in the CSSD decontamination room?

options.A: Waterproof gowns, utility gloves, and face shields
options.B: Dust masks and cotton lab coats
options.C: Sterile surgical gloves and sterile cloth gowns only
options.D: Lead aprons and radiation dosimeter badges

explanation: Decontamination staff deal with splashes of dirty water, blood, and harsh chemicals, so waterproof gear and face shields are essential to stay safe. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h8)

question: Besides physical safety, what else helps create a healing ward environment?

options.A: Playing loud music to keep patients awake during the day
options.B: Keeping the lights at maximum brightness twenty-four hours a day
options.C: Allowing visitors to stay without any time limits
options.D: Reducing noise and addressing patient grievances promptly

explanation: You've got this! Healing isn't just physical—lowering stress by keeping noise down and listening to patient complaints makes a huge difference. [learn more](GST321_U6_T2#GST321_U6_T2_h6)

question: Why is the alkaline nature of the fluid from the bulbourethral glands important?

options.A: It stimulates the testes to release more testosterone
options.B: It creates a thick clot to block the vaginal opening
options.C: It freezes sperm to preserve them until intercourse
options.D: It neutralizes leftover acid from urine in the urethra

explanation: Urine leaves acid traces in the urethra that can harm sperm, so the alkaline mucus neutralizes them first. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T3#GNS121_U4_T3_h4)

question: As a nurse, what is the most important first step when caring for a pregnant teenager?

options.A: Isolating her from her family members
options.B: Putting her on strict dietary restriction
options.C: Reporting her immediately to child welfare authorities
options.D: Building a trusting, non-judgmental therapeutic relationship

explanation: Spot on! Teens are often afraid of being scolded. Building trust makes them feel safe to come to the clinic and share what they need. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T8#GNS312_U3_T8_h6)

question: Why do doctors evaluate fertility after just six months for women aged thirty-five and older?

options.A: The uterine lining becomes too thick for implantation over time
options.B: Ovarian reserve and egg quality naturally decrease faster at this age
options.C: Hormonal contraceptives take longer to leave the body after age thirty-five
options.D: Older women have a higher rate of chronic pelvic infections

explanation: A quicker evaluation is helpful because a woman's egg quality and supply naturally start to decline faster in her late thirties. Keep up the good work! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T23#GNS312_U1_T23_h1)

question: What is the primary benefit of involving local community leaders when planning a health education program?

options.A: It creates a sense of community ownership and cooperation
options.B: It allows the nurse to take a long holiday from clinical duties
options.C: It ensures the nurse receives a personal financial bonus
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any teaching materials

explanation: When local leaders are involved from the start, the community is much more likely to trust the nurse and adopt the recommended health practices. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T1#GNS214_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is the main reason for putting an artificial airway in an unconscious patient?

options.A: To prevent the tongue from sliding back during feeding
options.B: To allow the administration of oral liquid medications
options.C: To protect against aspiration and maintain clear breathing
options.D: To measure core body temperature continuously

explanation: You're doing great! Unconscious patients can't protect their airway or swallow properly, so a tube keeps air flowing and stops saliva or vomit from entering the lungs. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T9#GNS123_U3_T9_h7)

question: What is the main point of the evaluation phase in your care plan?

options.A: To determine if the patient has met the established clinical goals
options.B: To assign nursing duties for the upcoming morning shift
options.C: To write a formal letter of discharge for the patient's family
options.D: To calculate the total financial cost of hospital treatment

explanation: Evaluation is just checking your report card: did the patient reach the goals we set earlier? It helps us see if our nursing care paid off. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T8#GNS321_U2_T8_h6)

question: How does qualitative data analysis differ from quantitative analysis?

options.A: Qualitative analysis looks for recurring themes in text rather than numbers
options.B: Qualitative analysis ignores patient words and focuses on lab values
options.C: Qualitative analysis uses computer software to run complex regressions
options.D: Qualitative analysis requires strict mathematical proof of significance

explanation: Instead of crunching numbers, qualitative researchers read through text to find common patterns and themes in what people said. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T6#GNS224_U1_T6_h6)

question: Why would a doctor perform a lumbar puncture (spinal tap) when investigating suspected disseminated sclerosis?

options.A: To drain excess blood following an acute head injury
options.B: To check cerebrospinal fluid for signs of abnormal immune activity
options.C: To inject medication that stops nerve pain immediately
options.D: To measure the exact pressure inside the heart chambers

explanation: Testing the spinal fluid helps find specific markers (like oligoclonal bands) that point straight to inflammation in the central nervous system. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is a frequent cause of a false-positive Mantoux test in individuals from other countries?

options.A: Prior vaccination with the BCG vaccine
options.B: Having a severe viral cold during testing
options.C: Receiving the injection too deep in the skin
options.D: Taking daily multi-vitamin supplements

explanation: The BCG vaccine, given in many countries to prevent childhood TB, can cause the immune system to react to PPD, creating a false-positive skin test. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h7)

question: Why is the skin considered our body's primary shield?

options.A: It sits right between our internal organs and the outside world.
options.B: It produces all our red blood cells.
options.C: It pumps nutrients directly into underlying muscles.
options.D: It filters waste straight out of our bloodstream.

explanation: Spot on! Because skin covers our entire outside, it acts as our very first line of defense against everyday hazards. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T3#GNS211_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why is Small Cell Lung Cancer usually treated with medications (systemic therapy) rather than surgery right away?

options.A: It only occurs in patients who are too old for operations.
options.B: It grows extremely slowly inside the main bronchial tubes.
options.C: It usually spreads to other body parts very early before detection.
options.D: It is completely resistant to any form of surgical removal.

explanation: Great thinking! Small cell lung cancer grows fast and tends to spread (metastasize) early, meaning surgery alone usually isn't enough to catch it all. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h1)

question: An injured survivor of an assault arrives at your facility. What is your very first clinical priority?

options.A: Conducting a detailed psychological interview
options.B: Filing mandatory police incident reports
options.C: Collecting forensic swabs and clothing fibers
options.D: Stabilizing life-threatening physical injuries

explanation: Saving a life and stabilizing the patient always comes first before collecting evidence or paperwork. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T13#GNS312_U4_T13_h4)

question: As a nurse, what is a crucial check to make *before* a patient goes for a liver biopsy?

options.A: Check that clotting blood tests are safe and consent is signed
options.B: Perform a minor surgery to drain belly fluid
options.C: Give them strong general anesthesia right in the ward
options.D: Make sure they eat a large heavy meal

explanation: Spot on! Safety first—always verify clotting labs and make sure the patient understands and signs the consent form before the procedure. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T10#GNS221_U2_T10_h3)

question: Which of these best captures the full picture of injection safety?

options.A: It is limited to washing hands before opening a packaged syringe
options.B: It covers everything from deciding on the route to safe disposal of waste
options.C: It focuses solely on preventing needlestick injuries among medical doctors
options.D: It only refers to the exact moment the needle enters the patient's skin

explanation: Injection safety isn't just one quick action. It's a complete journey—from checking if the injection is needed, to giving it cleanly, to throwing away the sharps properly. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h2)

question: Why is it so important to involve the family when planning care for an elderly Nigerian patient?

options.A: Family members must pay all hospital bills in advance
options.B: Hospital policies forbid nurses from talking directly to patients
options.C: Relatives are legally required to administer all medications
options.D: Families provide the primary support network upon discharge

explanation: Brilliant! Because family care is at the heart of our society, partnering with relatives ensures the patient gets the best support possible once they leave the hospital. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T4#GNS321_U3_T4_h7)

question: Why might a cancer care plan shift from trying to cure the disease to focusing purely on comfort and palliation?

options.A: Standard surgical options are suddenly much safer than outpatient chemotherapy.
options.B: The patient's insurance policy has expired and can no longer cover active medications.
options.C: The nursing staff prefers managing comfort care over administering toxic drugs.
options.D: The disease has progressed beyond the point where a cure or control is realistically achievable.

explanation: Spot on! When the disease advances past where treatment can stop it, the healthcare team shifts gears to palliation—focusing entirely on comfort, symptom relief, and quality of life. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h1)

question: Which lab test is used to monitor a patient taking the blood thinner warfarin?

options.A: Prothrombin Time and INR
options.B: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate
options.C: Activated partial thromboplastin time
options.D: Full blood count with differential

explanation: PT and INR are the go-to tests to make sure a patient on warfarin is getting just the right dose—not too thick, not too thin! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T5#GNS311_U2_T5_h5)

question: What is a common misunderstanding caregivers have about normal vaccine reactions?

options.A: Total absence of any reaction proves the vaccine failed to work
options.B: Crying after an injection means the child has developed an allergy
options.C: Mild fever and swelling mean the child is harmed and should skip future doses
options.D: A slight rash indicates the child is now immune to all known diseases

explanation: You're doing great! Parents sometimes mistake normal, mild immune responses like a low-grade fever for a dangerous sickness and skip the next shots. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T69#GNS214_U1_T69_h6)

question: What is the main underlying issue in a patient with gastroparesis?

options.A: Severe inflammation and sores in the small bowel lining
options.B: Delayed stomach emptying even though there is no physical blockage
options.C: A total loss of the protective mucus barrier in the stomach
options.D: Food moving so fast it goes straight into the colon

explanation: In gastroparesis, the stomach is just too slow at emptying its contents. There's no tumor or physical blockage—it's usually a muscle or nerve issue! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T10#GNS213_U3_T10_h4)

question: Why is the 'typical use' failure rate for condoms higher than the 'perfect use' rate?

options.A: Incompatible blood types between partners
options.B: User errors like inconsistent use or breakage
options.C: Manufacturing defects in the factory
options.D: Natural expiration of latex while in the box

explanation: Spot on! In the real world, mistakes happen—like not wearing it every time or putting it on late—which lowers effectiveness compared to lab tests. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h6)

question: A pregnant patient at 28 weeks suddenly has high blood sugar. Which hormone naturally causes the metabolic stress that brought this to light?

options.A: Human placental lactogen
options.B: Prolactin
options.C: Oxytocin
options.D: Aldosterone

explanation: Spot on! hPL causes normal insulin resistance. If the mother's pancreas can't pump out enough extra insulin to match this, it leads to gestational diabetes. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T14#GNS121_U5_T14_h5)

question: Why is it important for nurses to remove contaminated clothing and wash a poisoned patient's skin right away?

options.A: To prevent secondary exposure and contamination of healthcare staff
options.B: To ensure the laboratory test results are not ruined by skin oils
options.C: To comply with legal paperwork requirements for hazardous waste
options.D: To speed up the chemical breakdown of the poison inside the body

explanation: Decontamination protects you too! We want to make sure the poison doesn't transfer from the patient onto the healthcare workers. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T1#GNS215_U5_T1_h6)

question: What is the universal physical sign that someone is choking?

options.A: Waving both arms in the air rapidly
options.B: Holding the stomach and bending forward
options.C: Clutching the throat with one or both hands
options.D: Pointing to the left side of the chest

explanation: When someone's airway is blocked, they will instinctively clutch their throat with one or both hands. It's a universal distress signal! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T6#GNS321_U2_T6_h6)

question: Why might an elderly patient with a severe bacterial infection not run a high fever?

options.A: Older adults naturally maintain a much higher internal baseline temperature
options.B: The aging immune system has a blunted inflammatory and febrile response
options.C: Lung tissue infections never trigger body temperature changes at any age
options.D: Circulating white blood cells destroy all heat-producing chemicals instantly

explanation: Brilliant! Because of immunosenescence, older bodies often fail to mount a classic high fever, even when fighting a dangerous infection. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T2#GNS321_U3_T2_h6)

question: When is acute endometritis most commonly seen?

options.A: The first trimester of a normal pregnancy
options.B: The postpartum period following childbirth
options.C: The week immediately following menopause
options.D: The final days of a regular menstrual cycle

explanation: Spot on! After delivery, the uterus has a fresh healing wound where the placenta was attached, making it much easier for bacteria to take hold during the postpartum period. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T20#GNS216_U5_T20_h2)

question: What does the term 'rheumatism' mean in everyday clinical practice?

options.A: An acute injury sustained during heavy physical labor
options.B: A single bacterial infection of the bone marrow
options.C: A complete degeneration of spinal discs from sudden trauma
options.D: Any painful condition affecting joints, muscles, or bones

explanation: Think of rheumatism as a helpful umbrella term! It covers various aches and pains in the musculoskeletal system rather than pointing to just one specific disease. You've got this! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T12#GNS222_U1_T12_h1)

question: Which method of applying a painful stimulus is usually avoided in modern nursing because it causes unnecessary bruising?

options.A: Supraorbital pressure
options.B: Trapezius squeeze
options.C: Nail bed pressure
options.D: Sternal rub

explanation: Vigorous sternal rubbing (grinding knuckles on the chest bone) can leave nasty bruises and trauma. Safer methods like a trapezius squeeze are preferred today. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T6#GNS222_U3_T6_h5)

question: What main thing defines 'special groups' in community health?

options.A: Having a very high financial income
options.B: Belonging to a particular political party
options.C: Higher health risks and limited access to care
options.D: Living exclusively in capital cities

explanation: You nailed it! Special groups are populations that face higher health vulnerabilities and struggle more to get standard healthcare. Knowing who they are helps us direct our care where it's needed most. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T26#GNS225_U5_T26_h1)

question: Which of these common substances acts as a Central Nervous System (CNS) depressant?

options.A: Amphetamine
options.B: Nicotine
options.C: Alcohol
options.D: Cocaine

explanation: Correct! Alcohol slows down brain activity, making it a depressant. Remember: depressants slow things down, while stimulants speed them up. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T5#GNS223_U6_T5_h3)

question: In the emergency ABCDE primary survey, what does the letter 'A' stand for?

options.A: Antibiotic
options.B: Anxiety
options.C: Airway
options.D: Activity

explanation: Easy and essential! Checking and clearing the airway is always the number one priority in any emergency. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T5#GNS221_U3_T5_h3)

question: Which imaging test is the absolute go-to choice for getting a clear picture of brain and spinal tumors?

options.A: Magnetic Resonance Imaging
options.B: Bone densitometry scan
options.C: Standard chest X-ray
options.D: Abdominal ultrasound

explanation: Spot on! MRI gives doctors the sharpest, most detailed look at soft tissues like the brain and spinal cord, making it the favorite tool for spotting nervous system growths. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T14#GNS222_U3_T14_h4)

question: What is the key feature of a focal aware seizure?

options.A: The patient remains fully conscious during the event
options.B: Both hemispheres of the brain are involved simultaneously
options.C: The episode lasts for longer than thirty continuous minutes
options.D: The patient experiences a complete loss of motor function

explanation: In a focal aware seizure, the electrical activity stays in one area, and the patient stays awake and aware of what is happening. Keep up the great studying! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T9#GNS222_U4_T9_h3)

question: Why is it much harder to get an exact, consistent dose from herbal medicines compared to factory-made tablets?

options.A: Government regulations strictly forbid the weighing of plant roots
options.B: Active ingredient levels vary based on soil, weather, and plant maturity
options.C: Herbal remedies lose all chemical potency within two hours of harvest
options.D: Traditional healers refuse to use measuring spoons and cups

explanation: Mother Nature doesn't use a laboratory scale! Plants grow differently depending on the soil and weather, meaning the strength of the active ingredients changes from one harvest to the next. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T2#GNS125_U2_T2_h6)
